clue.text: Scratched old record?

parts.note: suggests a worn-out gramophone disc, but means a document whose writing was scraped off so the parchment could be reused

explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript whose earlier text was scraped away and written over is literally an old record that has been scratched out.

clue.text: Press promote and encourage enterprise

definitions.meaning: to press is to urge forward or shove
to back and drive something on
drive or energetic ambition, as in a person with plenty of get-up-and-go

explanation.surface: A newspaper is urged to back business initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions run together; 'Press' looks like the newspapers but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word covers shoving, backing a cause, and the go-getting drive of an ambitious person.

clue.text: White ill, out of order over a year

indicators.note: something out of order is jumbled up, so the letters of ill are rearranged

parts.note: Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A pale invalid feels unwell and broken for a whole year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' turns ILL into LIL; in a down clue 'over' puts it above Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower stands for whiteness, as in the phrase lily-white.

clue.text: This can give me Lisle's aria

definitions.text: This can give me Lisle's aria

indicators.note: the letters of the following words can be rearranged to give something new

parts.note: the possessive is spelt out here, its S counting as a letter

explanation.surface: A national song that is the work of the composer Rouget de Lisle.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the letters of ME LISLES ARIA are rearranged, and the whole clue describes the French anthem, written by Rouget de Lisle in 1792.
explanation.definitionFit: The French national anthem was composed by Rouget de Lisle, so it truly is his song.

clue.text: Spectacle for a great many

definitions.meaning: a show or something worth looking at

explanation.surface: A show staged for a huge crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a striking view and, informally, a large quantity.

clue.text: Does he play to the gallery in the evening performance?

definitions.text: Does he play to the gallery in the evening performance?

parts.words: Does he play to the gallery in the evening performance?
parts.note: seems to describe a showy actor in a night-time play, but pictures a suitor singing up to a balcony at night

explanation.definitionFit: A suitor who sings beneath a window or balcony at night plays to the gallery in an evening performance.

clue.text: Small drink stain

definitions.meaning: a little drop, as in a ... of whisky

explanation.surface: Spilling a little drink leaves a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a modest tot of liquor and a mark left on fabric.

clue.text: This ground will not thaw-farmers opt out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of farmers opt are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Farmers decline to work land that stays frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'opt out', but it rearranges FARMERS OPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that stays frozen through every season in polar regions is described here.

clue.text: Toddler and runner of course

definitions.meaning: a small child aged about two
a racehorse in its second year, running on a racecourse

explanation.surface: A small child and a racer, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means on a racecourse; horses of this age run in their own races.
explanation.definitionFit: A child of that age toddles, and racehorses of that age form a class of runners.

clue.text: Second eleven from Germany watch their inner pride

parts.note: elf is the German word for eleven
to regard is to watch or look at

explanation.surface: A reserve football side from Germany watches their pride in action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' looks like a reserve team, but splits into S and the German ELF.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem for oneself is a kind of inward vanity or conceit.

clue.text: River a fleet love to follow

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, the British fleet
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: A navy and a romance follow a river.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the river that flows through Florence and Pisa.

clue.text: Some grumbling about this condition?

parts.note: reads as patients complaining, but a 'grumbling' organ in the lower abdomen is the condition

explanation.definitionFit: A grumbling appendix is the name for a mild, recurring inflammation of that organ.

clue.text: Formation of pelagic terns landing

indicators.note: a formation is an arrangement, so the letters of pelagic terns are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Seabirds flying in formation come in to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formation' looks like birds flying in a pattern, but rearranges PELAGIC TERNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair landing is a spot where a climber can pause, so it is somewhere to stop and rest.

clue.text: Selection for mixed sets

definitions.meaning: a range or variety on offer
collections of various kinds put together

explanation.surface: Choosing between jumbled sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety on offer, like a box of different chocolates, is both a choice and a mixed collection.

clue.text: Religious belief that followed Emma's coming out

definitions.meaning: Jane Austen's novel published after Emma

explanation.surface: A faith that arose after a woman's debut in society.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Austen's last completed novel appeared after her Emma; 'coming out' means publication, not a debutante's debut.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a creed, and is also the title of the Austen novel published after Emma.

clue.text: Weighing-machine could be set early to take old penny

indicators.note: says the letters of set early could be arranged differently

parts.note: D was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A scale could be set up early to take an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges SET EARLY into STEELYAR, which then takes D, the old penny before decimal coinage in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a balance with a sliding weight on a lever arm, used for weighing goods.

clue.text: A 2p picker-up is one who would value it

parts.note: two of the letter P, read cryptically
a raiser is one who lifts or picks something up

explanation.surface: Someone who picks up a two-pence coin knows its worth.
explanation.walkthrough: '2p' looks like two pence but is read as P twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuer assesses what an item is worth.

clue.text: Blunder here yet panic does not begin

indicators.note: the word for panic loses its first letter, so it does not begin

parts.note: terror is extreme fear or panic

explanation.surface: A mistake made here, yet nobody starts to panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake or slip is a gaffe.

clue.text: Alternative easier part of Rossi aria…

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An opera song by Rossi has a simpler version.
explanation.walkthrough: In music the term marks an easier alternative passage printed in a score.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term for a simpler optional passage offered in place of a harder one.

clue.text: … rather like Bliss?

parts.note: continues from the clue before, as if describing a song by the composer Arthur Bliss, but means heavenly

explanation.definitionFit: Being heavenly is like perfect happiness, the bliss of the Garden of Eden.

clue.text: Clarity of photograph

definitions.meaning: being see-through or easy to understand
a slide, a positive image on film viewed with light behind it

explanation.surface: The sharpness of a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both see-through clearness and a photographic slide viewed against light.

clue.text: Mysterious how watercourse ends in lake

indicators.note: the end of the word watercourse supplies its final letter

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Strange how a stream finishes up in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncanny or spooky is strange and unsettling.

clue.text: Double note from Rudolph's girl

indicators.note: double means the note is written twice in a row

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A two-note phrase sung by Rudolph's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolph's girl is the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème, loved by the poet Rodolfo (Rudolph).
explanation.definitionFit: In La Bohème the seamstress loved by the poet Rodolfo is named so.

clue.text: Magistrate's bill

definitions.meaning: British slang for a judge or justice of the peace

explanation.surface: A judge's invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like an invoice but is a bird's bill; the 's is 'is', linking the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a justice of the peace this, and it is also a bird's mouth.

clue.text: Heroic record set by Olympic finalists

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the final letters of Olympic are taken

explanation.surface: A heroic record set by Olympic finalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and heroic in scale, like a long poem of heroes.

clue.text: Simenon's bureau, for example, with its back to the wall

definitions.text: Simenon's bureau, for example, with its back to the wall

parts.words: Simenon's bureau, for example, with its back to the wall
parts.note: sounds like Maigret's police bureau under pressure, but describes a writer's desk standing against a wall

explanation.definitionFit: It is a writing desk, the sort a novelist like Georges Simenon would write at, usually set against a wall.

clue.text: Lean nurse

definitions.meaning: to incline or have a tendency

explanation.surface: A thin carer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to incline towards something and to care for someone.

clue.text: Early break — place for putting glue

parts.note: a golf green is where a player putts
to stick is to glue

explanation.surface: A golfer's early break from the course to fix something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early break' is a fracture in a child, whose bones bend and crack on one side like a young twig.
explanation.definitionFit: This incomplete fracture occurs in the soft bones of young children, so it is a break early in life.
